Detailed method

Hard rolls. Currently 500 g flour, 58% hydration, 0% starter, 2% salt, and 0.8% yeast. That is 290 g water, 10 g salt, and 4 g yeast, 804 g of dough. Currently 8 rolls of 100.5 g each. These times assume you only change the flour amount and keep the percentages the same. Still judge the dough by how it looks and feels.

  1. Mix Stir 500 g flour, 290 g water, 10 g salt, and 4 g instant yeast until no dry flour remains, then knead 8 minutes until smooth. At 58% the dough is firm. Aim for about 24°C (75°F).
  2. Bulk Cover it at about 24°C (75°F) for 60 to 90 minutes. With 0.8% yeast it should grow by about half.
  3. Shape Divide the 804 g into 8 pieces of 100.5 g each. Tighten each piece into a round. The default 804 g uses a rimmed tray about 40 cm long, 30 cm wide, and 2 cm high. If you change the amount, use a tray sized to fit, or bake in batches.
  4. Proof Cover them for 30 to 50 minutes, until slightly puffy. Do not let them get soft and slack.
  5. Bake Heat the oven to 230°C (450°F). Bake 14 to 18 minutes with steam, until the crust is golden and firm. If you have no steam, set a small tray of hot water on the bottom rack. Cool on a rack.
